---
title: "Why Terrapinalytics?"
date: 2026-11-20
categories: [site-notes]
---

For over a decade, I’ve built little pet projects inspired by the likes of FiveThirtyEight, KenPom, and all sorts of analytics communities online. I like to engage with the world through data and economics, and I’ve generally expressed that through college sports with a Maryland flair.

Many of the projects on this site began in college on a random Google Sheet. The earliest ones were copied data and a few rudimentary Excel formulas. Some later ones dabbled in web scraping and programming languages as I tried to learn new skills the old-fashioned way. Few ever saw the light of day and most were limited by my own abilities. Terrapinalytics is an opportunity for me to revisit some of those, expand on them in ways I previously couldn’t, and maybe learn a few new skills along the way.

It’s 2026 and so many things on the internet *feel* AI-generated. A big part of me worries we’re barreling towards a world full of low-effort slop that seems pretty likely to disrupt many career paths. But the optimistic side of me is excited to pursue those opportunities I never had the time or ability for. So I’m going to lean into that and bring those projects to life with the help of AI. I’ve only got so much spare time, and the robots haven’t taken my day job just yet. But I want to do this with a level of quality I’d stand behind in my own work. I want the analysis here to reflect my own interests and judgments and to see where this next little pet project goes.
